items.title: NVIDIA tackles deepfakes and opens the door to AI agents at SIGGRAPH 2026
items.excerpt: At SIGGRAPH 2026 NVIDIA unveiled a Synthetic Video Detector NIM microservice that scores footage frame-by-frame so newsrooms and VFX teams can flag AI-generated clips, while showing how Adobe, Blender, Unreal, Boris FX Silhouette and Houdini are opening to AI agents via Model Context Protocol. A concrete look at how AI moves into both the authentication and the driving of creative pipelines.

items.title: Autodesk Adds AI and 3DGS Tools Across Maya, 3ds Max and More
items.excerpt: At SIGGRAPH 2026 Autodesk added a 'Bring Your Own Data' feature to Maya's MotionMaker, letting studios train custom generative motion models on their own rigs and mocap, plus editable 3D Gaussian splats in 3ds Max for folding AI-captured environments into shots. A craft-level shift in how animators and VFX artists generate and edit performance and scenes.

items.title: Is this the future of filmmaking?
items.excerpt: Damian Allen walks through a hybrid AI film-set approach built on Beeble's SwitchLight, where AI transforms backgrounds and relighting while real actor performances and camera work are preserved -- a middle ground between traditional production and fully synthetic generation. A hands-on read on how AI relighting reshapes the on-set and post workflow.

items.title: Puget Systems at SIGGRAPH 2026: an immersive Robo Dojo
items.excerpt: Puget Systems' SIGGRAPH 2026 'Robo Dojo' turns attendees into real-time MetaHuman avatars battling AI robots using LiDAR scanning and LED-volume virtual production, a live demo of markerless motion capture and real-time rendering feeding a game-engine pipeline. A tactile snapshot of where performance capture and virtual production are heading for film.

items.title: Puget Systems' Robo Dojo proves SIGGRAPH attendees have all the fun
items.excerpt: RedShark's take on Puget Systems' SIGGRAPH 2026 Robo Dojo, where visitors drive a MetaHuman in real time to fight AI robots through body movement, showcasing advances in markerless motion capture and real-time virtual production. (Same event as the ProVideo item -- included as an outlet alternative; dedup to one.)
